newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 3.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Thursday:
* The Federal Communications Commission said it planned to temporarily stop collecting payments on over $10 billion worth of wireless communications licenses sold at auction last year.
* Federal health officials said strawberries imported from Mexico and processed in California have caused 153 cases of hepatitis A infection among schoolchildren and teachers in Michigan.
* New York Governor George Pataki plans to commit $100 million in state funds towards building a waterfront park on New York City's Hudson River shoreline.
* News Analysis: With escalating violence in the Middle East, there is talk of bypassing the Oslo peace process.
* President Clinton and Vice President Al Gore received minute details of the Democratic Party's fund-raising in 1996 via a steady stream of memorandums.
* A Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center volunteer sent a chain letter which reached as far as Elizabeth Taylor and raised over $250,000.
* Traditional Christianity, no longer a persecuted faith, is fading in Japan.
